slides.title: Fleet is built in
slides.html: The connector works with Fleet as it comes. Another MDM needs a plugin, a small add-on that speaks to that MDM, and none exists yet.

slides.title: What an MDM must do
slides.html: An MDM fits if it can do these five things. Ask your MDM's vendor, or try them in its console.

slides.title: A group of its own
slides.html: Phones for one Deploy App enrol into one group, named after your deployment, such as golden-monkey DeployApp, with its own enrolment link.

slides.title: One challenge for all phones
slides.html: The MDM sends each phone's certificate request to Deploy App's SCEP URL, with the challenge you give it: the same for every phone.

slides.title: A name for each phone
slides.html: The certificate's name comes from a field you can set for each phone. That name is the phone's callsign.

slides.title: A new challenge each time
slides.html: Every opening makes a new challenge. If the MDM cannot take it from the connector, the phones view shows it for you to copy into the MDM, as with this demo plugin.

slides.title: Asking again
slides.html: After naming, the MDM must ask that one phone for its certificate again, and leave the others alone.

slides.title: Adding a plugin
slides.html: Technical staff add a plugin with the install line in the connector's README. With more than one MDM installed, the connector asks Which MDM?

slides.title: The connector asks first
slides.html: A plugin sees your MDM token. The first time you choose one, and after it is updated, the connector says which package it comes from and asks before using it.

slides.title: Steps by hand
slides.html: What the MDM cannot do by API, the connector lists for you to do in its console. Then press Show the phones.
